title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context from the previous page: a 'syntaxe', renamed 'spatio' here (axioms Spt 1-3 = Synt 1-3), is a triple (Σ, ≤, C). Its axioms say three things. (i) ≤ is a complete lattice order. (ii) C is an order-reversing involution, so C is a De Morgan involution and C0=1, C1=0. (iii) x ∧ Cx = 0, equivalently x ∨ Cx = 1. In modern terms this is a complete ortholattice.

On this page Grothendieck equips a spatio with its canonical 'disjonction': x |0| y :⟺ x ≤ Cy (⟺ y ≤ Cx by Spt 2). This is the orthogonality relation of an ortholattice.

He records that the relation is hereditary downward: x|0|y, x'≤x, y'≤y ⟹ x'|0|y'. A top-left marginal NB records compatibility with arbitrary sups: if x = sup x_i, y = sup y_j and x_i|0|y_j for all i,j, then x|0|y.

A crossed-out passage shows he intended to reconstruct (≤, C) from |0|. That is done on the next page (Prop. 1 and the Scholie).

Example. Let E = (E, |0|) be a set with a 'disjonction'. Disj 1 is symmetry. Disj 2 apparently says that self-disjoint elements, forming E_0, are disjoint from everything. Then Σ_E, the set of subsets A with A = cos-W(cos-W(A)), ordered by ⊂ and with C = cos-W, is a spatio. Here cos-W(A) = A^⊥ = {y : y|0|a for all a ∈ A}.

- Spt 1 and Spt 2 are the standard facts for the closed sets of the Galois connection given by a symmetric relation (Birkhoff polarity).
- Spt 3 follows from Disj 2. For any A, A ∩ A^⊥ ⊂ E_0. For closed A, since E_0 = E^⊥ is the bottom closed set, A ∩ A^⊥ = E_0 = 0_Σ.

Finally, the canonical map α_E : E → Σ_E is presumably x ↦ {x}^⊥⊥. The next page uses, for E = Σ itself, σ(x) = ↓x with inverse S ↦ sup S. This gives the representation of every complete ortholattice as the lattice of biorthogonally closed sets of its own orthogonality relation. The oblique bottom-left marginal sketches a generalisation to 'ensembles ordonnés disjonctifs' (E, ≤, |0|) with the same hereditary axiom, and a map E → Σ_E.

Purpose: to set up a duality between 'spatios' (complete ortholattices) and 'disjonction' structures, apparently as a foundation for the 'Ateliers' chapter.
errors: No mathematical errors on what is legible. The proofs of Spt 1-3 for Σ_E are only sketched.
Spt 3 needs Disj 2 interpreted as 'x|0|x ⟹ x|0|y for all y' (so that E_0 = E^⊥ is the bottom closed set). This interpretation is inferred, since Disj 2 is not stated on this page.
Transcription and wording variants: the line reads 'est un [ensemble à] disjonctions'. The neighbouring page's 'disposition' is almost certainly 'disjonction'.

deep.surprise_reason: The page rederives standard material on complete ortholattices and orthogonality spaces (Birkhoff polarities, MacLaren 1964, Dacey/Foulis–Randall). The only nonstandard touch is allowing a set E_0 of self-disjoint 'null' elements, a minor variant. It is mildly interesting biographically that Grothendieck developed this in 1986, but there is nothing new mathematically.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'À un spatio est [-associé-] {+muni+} d'une structure de disjonction canonique' is consistent with the image. The struck word sits above 'muni', and the leading letter is overwritten.
'Si E = (E,|0|) est un disjonctions' should likely read 'est un ensemble à disjonction' (or a similar noun); one word is garbled.
'cos-W^0_E(A)' with superscript ° in the first formula and 'cos-W_E(A)' in the second are as written. They denote the disjoint complement (orthogonal) of A.
The marginal NB at top left reads approximately: 'NB Si x = sup x_i, y = sup y_j, x_i|0|y_j ∀ i,j ⟹ x|0|y'.
